rationale: Needs both Talarico (TX) and El-Sayed (MI) to win per AP. Texas polls show Talarico +0 to +3 (Fox tie, UH 48-46, Marist 47-45), but Texas polls have historically overstated Democrats, so ~0.48; Michigan polls show El-Sayed +2 to +5 with Cook Toss-Up, ~0.68. Outcomes are positively correlated through the national environment, giving a joint ~0.38.

Minnesota has not elected a Republican senator since 2002 (base rate strongly D). Flanagan leads Tafoya by 3-5 points in averages (RCP +3.4, Pollsmax +4.6) in a Democratic-leaning national environment, though Cook moved it to Lean D and undecideds are high. Tightening is the main risk.

Resolves YES only on a 25bp deposit-rate hike on Oct 29. The ECB hiked to 2.50% in September; Reuters-polled economists and previews widely expect a pause in October with the next hike in December, as October has no new staff projections. A surprise hike is possible given 3.8% inflation but very unlikely. A search result showed a prediction-market price, which was discarded.

Needs no Israeli or Iranian air/missile strike impacting the other's territory through Nov 15. The ceasefire is fragile: US and Israel threaten renewed strikes and talks are stalled, but reports say Trump blocked renewed strikes before the Nov 3 midterms and Netanyahu would not strike before Israel's Oct 27 election. The main risk is a post-midterm resumption in the Nov 4-15 window; tanker and Houthi actions do not count.

South Carolina is strongly Republican (base rate very high), but this is an unusual race: appointed Sen. Darline Graham Nordone leads Annie Andrews by only 1-3 points in averages, and Andrews has a huge fundraising edge in a Democratic-leaning year. Partisan lean and polling still favor the Republican, but the margin is thin.

Ohio has trended Republican and polls overstated Democrats there in 2020 and 2024. Still, Acton leads Ramaswamy by about 3-4 points in averages (Marist +7, Fox +2, BGSU +6), and Sabato moved the race to Lean D. Adjusting for Ohio's polling bias leaves a modest Acton edge.

Non-market models mostly favor Democrats for the Senate: Silver Bulletin D 76%, DDHQ D 56%, Call the Map D 55%, Poliwave D 57%; Pollsmax is the outlier at R 54.5%. Close races in AK, TX, MI, MN and SC make it competitive, so R control is about 0.37. A search result quoted prediction-market prices, which were discarded.

Needs a general mutually agreed ceasefire by Oct 31. Only a local humanitarian truce in Oleshky has been agreed (it does not qualify), the next talks are set for mid-November in Abu Dhabi, and the Kremlin says combat operations continue. Five days remain.

Incumbent senators usually win, and Alaska leans R. However, Peltola narrowly leads in averages (DDHQ +2.4, RCP +0.8, NYT/Siena +7, Rasmussen Sullivan +1), wins the simulated RCV rounds, and holds a large money advantage. Sullivan is a modest underdog. A search result mentioned a prediction-market price, which was discarded.

Needs an official anthropic.com/news Fable 5.5 announcement by Oct 31 PST. Leaks suggest it is imminent: an Azure/LiteLLM model ID, partner-access reports, and TestingCatalog saying 'next week'. The Information reported a new Anthropic model this month but said the family is unclear. With only 5 days left and no official confirmation, this is roughly a coin flip. A search result quoted a prediction-market figure, which was discarded.

YES = no US-Iran Hormuz agreement announced by Nov 2. The June interim deal collapsed, Iran conditions reopening on ending the US blockade (which Trump rejects), an IRGC outlet denied a new proposal, and Trump is openly weighing strikes. Formal acceptance by both sides within about 7 days is unlikely, though Trump's pre-midterm 'big beautiful agreement' talk is a tail risk.

Needs both Saudi Arabia and the Houthis to announce a ceasefire agreement by Oct 31. Fighting is active, with Houthi barrages on Saudi cities on Oct 25 and an airport strike. There is a reported but unconfirmed $1B Iran-brokered offer, while Riyadh publicly rejects a new ceasefire without territorial concessions. Five days remain.
